title: SIG/CAIQ evidence accelerator and attestation delivery playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable, audit-ready playbook and a pre-packaged evidence bundle to accelerate responses to SIG/CAIQ and related customer security questionnaires. The playbook will be structured to support three delivery tiers aligned to pricing/packaging experiments: Starter (self-serve evidence index), Preferred (curated evidence bundle + one-hour review), and Enterprise (attestation + signed evidence + dedicated CE coordination).

Context and goals:
- Procurement cycles for enterprise customers are lengthened by ad-hoc evidence requests; sales and legal estimate 2–8 weeks saved per account if we can deliver a standardized bundle with clear SLAs.
- This work sits at the intersection of pricing/packaging experiments and security questionnaire capabilities: we will pilot bundling attestation deliverables into SKU add-ons and measure impact on conversion and time-to-contract.
- Deliverables: playbook (Confluence), evidence index (static bundle of PDFs + links), templated SIG/CAIQ responses, a small automation to assemble customer-specific bundles, and a sales-facing FAQ and pricing SKU definitions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence playbook created with step-by-step runbook for each tier, owners, SLAs, escalation path, and required artefacts.
- Evidence index includes versioned copies of: SOC/ISO summaries (redacted), network diagrams, KMS/HSM descriptions, data retention policies, encryption-at-rest docs, third-party audits linkage, and runtime SLOs.
- A sample customer bundle can be generated in < 24h for Starter, < 3 business days for Preferred, and < 10 business days for Enterprise (with CE).
- Pricing SKUs defined and approved by Finance for the pilot; Sales enablement doc and one-pager prepared.
- Pilot launched with 3 named accounts and baseline metrics (time-to-contract, security-questionnaire closures, revenue uplift) instrumented in Gainsight/Looker.

Scope decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Full automation of SIG/CAIQ mapping is out of scope for the pilot (would add 4–6 weeks); instead we will provide a semi-automated generator that stitches approved artifacts and highlights fields that require manual confirmation.
- We will not create new signed legal attestations in-house for the pilot; Enterprise tier uses a combination of signed cover letters and guided CE review. Longer-term legal may require formal attestation artifacts.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Week 0–1: Finalize SKU tiering with Finance & Sales; draft playbook template.
2) Week 1–2: Curate evidence assets and canonical SIG/CAIQ mapping; store canonical PDFs in GDrive and create a public index page in Confluence.
3) Week 2–3: Build a simple Python script (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/security-evidence-assembler) that outputs a zipped bundle and a cover README; include checklist for Sales/CE.
4) Week 3–6: Run pilot with 3 accounts; collect metrics and feedback; iterate.
5) Week 6: Decide go/no-go for expanding SKU to wider customer base and linking to billing.

Testing and measurement:
- Baseline 1: time from first security questionnaire sent to legal-signature (TTC baseline).
- Baseline 2: number of follow-up evidence requests per questionnaire.
- Success metrics for pilot: median TTC reduced by >= 30% for Preferred/Enterprise, decrease in follow-up requests by >= 40%, and positive sales feedback for SKU clarity.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Legal requires formal attestation leading to manual work and delays. Mitigation: early Legal gating and a pre-approved cover letter template; flag accounts likely to require formal attestation during qualification.
- Risk: Evidence bundle becomes stale. Mitigation: assign owners for each doc with quarterly review reminders and automatic version tagging in Drive.

- Which attestation language can Legal pre-approve for cover letters? (Marco to provide list.)
